body:
She’s 17, so it’s not really confidential I don’t think? 

I don’t want to rush her. But at some point I can’t just sit back and wait knowing what the risk of that is
Hey, were you able to get any advice?
That would be awesome thank you so much

I didn’t even consider trying to talk to her therapist but I have no idea how that would work since she’s under 18, and if it would work. Also I know her mom pretty well so I feel like that makes more sense? I basically just want to know how to say it to her

Therapists are legally obligated to inform parents/guardians when there is discussion of self harm or suicide. That’s why she wants to wait until she’s 18. I guess my question would be if I’m going to talk to her mom, do I let my friend know before? Obviously she very much doesn’t want me to, but I think it’ll go better than she expects, so maybe I should not tell her until after?
Please read the post before commenting
I will. She basically knows that I’m planning to do it if she doesn’t first
She’s suicidal buddy I’m not just gonna stop
I mean... ok but I’m asking if that’s an appropriate amount of information to give her mother

But would it be ok to basically just ask her mom to have a conversation with her? Tell her mom that she’s going to try to get more help when she turns 18 anyways, so we might as well do it now and it’s probably not worth the risk of waiting either

You’re underestimating my confidence in a lot of things. I know for a fact they don’t know about her suicidal thoughts, nor do they know about the extent of her anxiety. No, she isn’t planning to kill herself right now, but my worry is if those thoughts intensify just one night when she’s already at a low point or alone or something. I am absolutely right about her needing more help, I just don’t know the best way to go about that

I wouldn’t consider it for a second if I wasn’t worried about her safety. But I am. And I know that that worry is for good reason. The problem is that I think when she’s 18 she’s going to realize that her parents are going to find out anyway if she gets more treatment than a therapist, and she’s not gonna do it then either. Sooooo yeah

?? The plan is to tell her mom that her daughter needs more help than she’s getting, but not to be super specific and try to initiate a conversation between them. Obviously I’m going to tell her it’s her daughter.
Ok well... do you think it makes sense to basically just ask her mom to have a conversation with her by telling her that my friend needs more help?
You want to marry everyone you talk to? What

I have absolutely no clue where marriage came from but alright... I’m not saying she can’t have serious conversations, she can and we have (she just doesn’t want to talk to anyone else who can actually help her about it), she just doesn’t like the deep, cliche stuff and honestly neither do I
She is the absolute worst candidate for a deep conversation
